notes: This page only shows a minifigure opening the box, looking at the pile of pieces, sorting them by colour, and starting to build. No pieces are placed.
The parts list (165 pieces, 58 lines) was received with this page. It will be used for piece types and colours on later pages.
Page 3 starts a small red truck, the first of several mini-builds in this set.
Step 1: a 1x2 plate. It looks clear or white in the picture, so I took it as Trans-Clear, the only 1x2 plate in the parts list with that look.

Step 2: two black clip plates (4081b) go on the two studs of the plate, one at each end, with the clip rings facing outward as wheels. I assumed these are 4081b because it is the only black part with a clip ring. The wheel clips are not joined to anything yet.
Step 3: a red 1x2 plate goes on top of the two black clip plates.

Step 4: four black round 1x1 plates (6141) are clipped onto the two clip plates as wheels. The picture shows two wheels at each end of the truck, so I gave each clip plate two wheels. I could not tell exactly how they sit, so this is a guess.

Step 5: the red flat piece looks like a Tile 1x2 with Groove (3069b), so I used that. It sits on the back stud of the red plate b4. The clear cheese slope (54200) sits on the front stud of b4 as the windscreen.
The wheels rest on nothing, so their rests_on is empty. They attach only through the clips.
Page 5 starts a second mini-build, a blue train engine.
Step 1: a blue 1x3 plate. Step 2: a black 1x1 plate goes on the middle stud, with a black clip plate (4081b) on each end stud. The clip rings stick out at the ends as wheels.

Step 3: one clear 1x2 plate and one clear 1x1 plate fill the three top studs. The picture does not show which end gets the 1x2, so I put it over one end clip and the centre plate, with the 1x1 over the other end clip.
The wheel clips are not joined to anything yet.

The unplaced-parts list looks out of step with what I recorded for the truck on the previous pages (for example it still shows 2 red 1x2 plates and drops a Blue cheese slope). I followed the pictures and did not try to match the list.

Step 4 (the picture shows a turn-over icon): four black round plates are clipped onto the two clip plates as wheels, two per clip, the same guess as for the truck. The model is turned over, so the blue 1x3 plate b11 ends up on top with its studs facing up.
Step 5: a white 1x4 brick sits on the three studs of the blue plate b11 and overhangs one stud at the front.

Step 6 first builds a small cab on its own: a blue 1x1 plate on a blue 1x2 plate, a blue cheese slope on the 1x1 plate, and a clear cheese slope on the other stud of the 1x2 plate. The cab then goes on the front of the white brick.
I assumed the cab's 1x2 plate rests only on the brick's overhanging fourth stud. That leaves the clear slope's stud with nothing under it. I have not recorded the cab as sitting on anything else.

Step 7: a white flat tile goes on top of the white brick b21. The cab already covers the brick's fourth stud, so I took the tile as a Tile 1x3 (63864) over the other three studs. It could be a 1x4 tile instead.

Steps 8 and 9: a Toys R Us logo sticker goes on each long side of the white brick. The picture turns the model over between the two sides. I recorded the sticker sheet once as b27 and joined it to the brick. The sheet will supply more stickers on later pages, so it may need more joins then.
The stickers go on the side of the white brick, which I took to be the surface they are shown on. They may cover the tile edge as well.
Page 8 starts the main model, the Toys R Us store. Step 1 is a black 4x10 base plate. It is the first piece of this model, so rests_on is empty.
Step 2: four dark grey 1x4 plates (3710) go around the edge of the black base plate b28, leaving a hollow in the middle. I could not read the exact layout from the picture.

Step 3: a white 2x4 plate (3020) fills the middle of the hollow, and three dark grey 2x2 plates go along the front edge. I took these as 3022, because the list has 4 grey 2x2 plates and the icon is a plain square.
The pictures do not show whether the step 3 plates also overlap the step 2 plates, so I listed only the base plate b28 under each piece.

Step 4: the second black 4x10 plate is added as a lower layer. The first base b28 and everything on it sits on top of b37, and b37 sticks out to the front and right. That is how I read the picture, where the new plate's studs show one level lower than the first plate's.
I have not changed b28's rests_on from the earlier page. The new plate b37 has nothing under it, so its rests_on is empty. The link between b28 and b37 is recorded in other_joins.

The unplaced-parts list suggests the four 1x4 plates from the previous page may have been Blue 3710 rather than Dark Bluish Gray, although the picture looks dark grey. I did not change the earlier entries.
Step 5: a tan 1x2 tile and two light grey jumper plates (3794b) go on the exposed front part of the lower black plate b37, between the grey 2x2 plates and the front edge.
Step 6: three green 1x1 plates and five light grey 1x1 tiles go along the front edge of b37, the green ones near the ends. I read it as a pavement or garden edge.
I put every piece on b37 only. The pictures do not show whether any of them also sit on the grey 2x2 plates from step 3.

Step 7 adds eight more pieces on the front part of the lower black plate b37: two tan 1x2 tiles (next to the earlier tan tile, they make a three-stripe walkway), two dark grey 1x2 tiles, two dark grey 1x3 tiles, and two green 1x3 plates (grass at the front corners).
I put every piece on b37 only. The pictures do not show exactly where each piece goes, and they do not show whether any of them also sit on the grey 2x2 plates from step 3.

Step 8: one dark grey 2x2 plate, three light grey 1x2 plates and two light grey 1x4 plates. I put the 2x2 and the two 1x4 plates on the upper base b28, and the three 1x2 plates on the lower plate b37. I could not read exact positions or what each piece overlaps from the pictures.

Step 9: two light grey 2x2 corner plates (2420) go on b28. Two reddish-brown round plates go on top of green 1x1 plates, one at the front-left corner and one at the back-right of the pavement. I took the two green 1x1 plates to be b41 and b42, but could not tell which of the three green plates each brown plate sits on.
The pictures do not show whether the step 8 and 9 pieces also overlap the earlier plates.

Step 10 adds two lime round plates, two yellow 1x1 plates, two clear 1x1 plates and one clear 1x2 plate. I took the clear pieces to be 3024 and 3023 in Trans-Clear, since the list has only that clear colour for those parts.

I put the lime plates on green pieces at the front corners, the yellow plates on the two light grey corner plates, and the clear plates on the light grey 1x2 plates at the front. This is a guess, because the picture is small and I could not tell exactly which piece each one sits on.
Step 11 builds a small stack three times: two clear 1x1 plates with a yellow 1x1 plate on top. One goes on the left of the building and two on the right. Each stack is one brick high.
Step 12 starts the back wall: a white 1x1 brick, a dark grey grille brick and a white 1x4 brick, all placed along the back row of the base.
The pictures do not show exactly which lower pieces each stack and wall piece sit on, so I picked the nearest plates from earlier pages. These links are guesses.
Step 13: a black 2x2 brick goes in the middle of the building, on the white plate area b33. A white Technic brick 1x2 with two pin holes goes at the left end, on the light grey plate b61.
I only listed the nearest plate under each brick. The black brick may also sit on other plates, which the picture does not show.
Step 14: a second white Technic brick 1x2 gets two black Technic pins pushed into its holes, then goes at the back-right corner of the building, with the pins sticking out sideways.
Step 15: two white 1x1 bricks go on at the right end of the back wall. I could not read exactly where, so I put them on the upper base b28. They may sit on other pieces as well.
The Technic brick is placed on b57, which is my guess at the plate in the back-right corner.
Step 16 builds a small stack: a red 1x2 plate, two clear 1x2 plates on it, and a red 1x2 tile on top. It then goes on the white plate b33, in front of the black 2x2 brick.
The picture shows two clear plates in the stack, but it is hard to tell whether the second one sits directly on the first. I assumed they stack directly.
Step 17 adds two blue 1x2 bricks, one on each side of the building (left front and right back), and two yellow 1x1 bricks, one on each side of the red counter.
Which plate each brick sits on is a guess. The blue bricks go on the two light grey corner plates, and the yellow bricks go on the white plate b33. The picture does not show the plates underneath.
Step 18 builds a stack of three clear 1x1 plates twice. One stack goes on the free stud of each blue 1x2 brick (b97 on the left, b98 on the right), the two spots the arrows point to.
I read the arrows as pointing at the blue bricks. The picture is small, so the exact spot could differ.
Step 19 adds two clear cheese slopes, two green flower plates and two green cones. The cones go on the two reddish-brown round plates as small trees. The flowers go on the two lime round plates.
The picture shows only one slope clearly, at the front-left on the clear plates. I put the second slope on the other clear 1x1 plate (b72). This is a guess.
Step 20 stacks two silver round plates and a silver round tile on top, like a short lamp post. It goes at the right of the front pavement.
I put it on the free stud of the right-hand light grey jumper plate b40. The picture does not make the exact spot clear, so that is a guess.
Step 21 lays the first roof layer: two white 2x4 plates (3020) at the left and right ends and one white 2x6 plate (3795) along the back.
The pictures do not show exactly which pieces each plate rests on, so I listed the wall pieces, towers and stacks nearest to it. Those lists are guesses.
Step 22: a yellow 1x4 tile bridges the two yellow 1x1 bricks over the red counter, like a shop entrance. Two blue 1x2 plates cap the blue bricks at the front.

I put each blue plate on its blue 1x2 brick (b97 on the left, b98 on the right). The clear plate stacks from step 18 sit on those same bricks, so the plates may in fact rest on the stacks instead. The picture does not settle this.
Step 23 puts a blue border on the white roof plates: two blue 1x4 plates and three blue 1x2 plates along the back, left and right edges.
The picture does not show exactly where each plate lies or what it overlaps, so the rests_on links are guesses. The blue plates go on the three white roof plates b116, b117 and b118.
Step 24 finishes the blue frame at the front of the roof: a blue 1x6 plate across the front, and a blue 2x2 corner plate at each front corner.

I read the 1x6 plate as resting on the two front blue plates and the yellow tile, and each corner plate as resting on a white roof plate plus the blue plate next to it. The picture does not make this certain, so these links are guesses.
Step 25 adds four white 1x4 bricks on top of the blue roof border, making a raised white wall along the left, back and right.
The exact layout is hard to read, so the rests_on links to the blue border plates (b122 to b126) are guesses.
Step 26 adds two tan 1x4 bricks side by side along the back, just inside the white wall.
I put both bricks on the white 2x6 roof plate b118. That is the nearest piece under them, but the picture could hide others.
The unplaced-parts list shows only one tan 1x4 brick fewer than before this page, but the picture clearly shows two being added. I followed the picture.
Step 27 adds a second blue layer at the front of the roof: a blue 2x2 corner plate at each front corner, and a blue 1x6 plate between them.

I put the corner plates on the first front corner plates and the 1x6 plate beneath them. The 1x6 plate's exact position and what it overlaps are not shown, so I listed only b129 under it. These links are guesses.
Step 28 adds three red door-rail plates (32028) across the front of the blue roof layer, and a blue 1x2 plate at each end of the front.
The picture shows only the right-hand blue plate being added, with the 2x label meaning another one on the left. I put the first on b136 and the second on b137.
The rests_on links are guesses based on where the pieces appear, because the pictures are small. I assumed the red plates sit on the blue 1x6 plate b138 and the corner plates.
Step 29 adds a blue 1x6 plate across the front on top of the red plates, two blue 1x4 plates along the back on the white bricks, and two green 1x3 plates, one at each side of the roof.
I read the green pieces as 1x3 plates (3623). The unplaced-parts list still shows 2 green 1x3 plates after this page, so the colour or type may differ from the picture. I followed the picture.
The rests_on links are my best guesses from the pictures, which are small.
Step 30 caps the white wall on the roof with tiles: one white 1x4 tile (2431) and four shorter white 1x3 tiles (63864).
I took the four smaller tiles as 1x3 because the icon is shorter than the 1x4 tile. Which white brick each tile covers is a guess, since the pictures are small.
The unplaced-parts list still shows 2 white 1x3 tiles after this page. I followed the picture.
Step 31 adds two blue 2x4 bricks (3001) and two blue 1x4 bricks with studs on the side (30414). The 2x4 bricks fill the roof, and the side-stud bricks go along the front.
The side studs of the 30414 bricks face outward and are not joined to anything yet, so I recorded no side joins.
The rests_on links are guesses from the small pictures.
Step 32 covers the roof with four blue 2x4 tiles in a 2x2 layout.

The picture does not show which lower bricks each tile covers, so the rests_on links are guesses. I assumed the back two tiles sit on the two 2x4 bricks and the front two straddle the side-stud bricks and the 2x4 bricks.
Step 33: a blue 1x4 tile gets a Toys R Us sticker, then goes sideways onto the four side studs of a front blue 1x4 stud-side brick, as the shop sign.
I chose b156 for the join, but the sign could be on b157 or span both. The picture does not say. The sticker comes from the sheet b27 recorded earlier.
The sign tile rests on nothing, so its rests_on is empty.
Step 34 builds a street lamp from a black round support (64644), a light round plate and a dark round plate. It goes at the front-right corner of the base.

Sub-step 1 shows the light round plate going straight onto the support, so I stacked it there and put the dark plate on top of it, as sub-step 2 seems to show. The light plate could instead be a Flat Silver 6141 or the round tile, but all of those are already used on the previous page, so I used the Trans-Clear 6141.
I put the lamp on the lower black plate b37, at the front-right. The exact stud under it is a guess.
This page only shows the finished store next to the small red truck and the blue train engine. No pieces are added.
The unplaced-parts list still shows a white 1x3 brick (3622) and a dark grey 1x4 plate (3710). The pages so far did not place either, so they may be on the last pages or be spare pieces.
This page is a photo of the finished Bricktober street, with the hotel, the station and the Toys R Us store side by side. It has no building step, so it adds nothing.
The white 1x3 brick (3622) and the dark grey 1x4 plate (3710) are still unplaced. Neither has appeared on any page so far.
This is the back cover. It shows the boxes of sets 40141, 40142, 40143 and 40144, the whole street, and the vehicles, plus the copyright line. There is no building step, so nothing is added.
The white 1x3 brick (3622) and the dark grey 1x4 plate (3710) were never placed on any page I was given, so they are probably spare pieces.

Separate groups: this is not a real error. The booklet builds three separate models: the small red truck (b1 to b10), the blue train engine (b11 to b27) and the Toys R Us store (b28 to b165). Page 37 shows them side by side, not joined. I added no connection between them.

The sticker sheet b27 is one physical part that supplies stickers for both the train engine and the store sign tile b162. That is the only link between those two models, so the checker counts them as one group. The truck is the second group. I kept the sticker links.

b129 and b119: this is a real error in my earlier entry. The yellow tile b119 (lego-2431) has no studs, so nothing can rest on it, and b129 should rest only on the blue plates b120 and b121, which are already in its rests_on list. The b119 entry should be ignored. I can only return additions, so I could not delete the edge.
Tiles are never a base for other pieces. Where I put pieces on tiles, the tile sits at the top of a stack, so I checked those and found no other cases.

Separate groups: I am keeping this as it is, because it is not a real error. Set 40144 builds three separate models, shown side by side on page 37: the red truck (b1 to b10), the blue train engine (b11 to b27) and the Toys R Us store (b28 to b165). Nothing in the booklet joins them, and a made-up connection would be wrong. The only link between two of them is the one sticker sheet b27, which supplies stickers for both the train engine and the store sign.

b129 on b119: this is a real error, but I cannot fix it with an addition. The yellow tile b119 (lego-2431) has no studs, so b129 cannot clutch it. b129 is held by the blue plates b120 and b121, which are already in its rests_on list. The b119 entry in b129's rests_on is wrong and should be dropped. I could only return additions, so the edge is still there.
I added nothing new, because both problems can only be fixed by removing or keeping existing entries.

notes: This page only shows a minifigure opening the box, looking at the pile of pieces, sorting them by colour, and starting to build. No pieces are placed.
The parts list (165 pieces, 58 lines) was received with this page. It will be used for piece types and colours on later pages.
Page 3 starts a small red truck, the first of several mini-builds in this set.
Step 1: a 1x2 plate. It looks clear or white in the picture, so I took it as Trans-Clear, the only 1x2 plate in the parts list with that look.

Step 2: two black clip plates (4081b) go on the two studs of the plate, one at each end, with the clip rings facing outward as wheels. I assumed these are 4081b because it is the only black part with a clip ring. The wheel clips are not joined to anything yet.
Step 3: a red 1x2 plate goes on top of the two black clip plates.

Step 4: four black round 1x1 plates (6141) are clipped onto the two clip plates as wheels. The picture shows two wheels at each end of the truck, so I gave each clip plate two wheels. I could not tell exactly how they sit, so this is a guess.

Step 5: the red flat piece looks like a Tile 1x2 with Groove (3069b), so I used that. It sits on the back stud of the red plate b4. The clear cheese slope (54200) sits on the front stud of b4 as the windscreen.
The wheels rest on nothing, so their rests_on is empty. They attach only through the clips.
Page 5 starts a second mini-build, a blue train engine.
Step 1: a blue 1x3 plate. Step 2: a black 1x1 plate goes on the middle stud, with a black clip plate (4081b) on each end stud. The clip rings stick out at the ends as wheels.

Step 3: one clear 1x2 plate and one clear 1x1 plate fill the three top studs. The picture does not show which end gets the 1x2, so I put it over one end clip and the centre plate, with the 1x1 over the other end clip.
The wheel clips are not joined to anything yet.

The unplaced-parts list looks out of step with what I recorded for the truck on the previous pages (for example it still shows 2 red 1x2 plates and drops a Blue cheese slope). I followed the pictures and did not try to match the list.

Step 4 (the picture shows a turn-over icon): four black round plates are clipped onto the two clip plates as wheels, two per clip, the same guess as for the truck. The model is turned over, so the blue 1x3 plate b11 ends up on top with its studs facing up.
Step 5: a white 1x4 brick sits on the three studs of the blue plate b11 and overhangs one stud at the front.

Step 6 first builds a small cab on its own: a blue 1x1 plate on a blue 1x2 plate, a blue cheese slope on the 1x1 plate, and a clear cheese slope on the other stud of the 1x2 plate. The cab then goes on the front of the white brick.
I assumed the cab's 1x2 plate rests only on the brick's overhanging fourth stud. That leaves the clear slope's stud with nothing under it. I have not recorded the cab as sitting on anything else.

Step 7: a white flat tile goes on top of the white brick b21. The cab already covers the brick's fourth stud, so I took the tile as a Tile 1x3 (63864) over the other three studs. It could be a 1x4 tile instead.

Steps 8 and 9: a Toys R Us logo sticker goes on each long side of the white brick. The picture turns the model over between the two sides. I recorded the sticker sheet once as b27 and joined it to the brick. The sheet will supply more stickers on later pages, so it may need more joins then.
The stickers go on the side of the white brick, which I took to be the surface they are shown on. They may cover the tile edge as well.
Page 8 starts the main model, the Toys R Us store. Step 1 is a black 4x10 base plate. It is the first piece of this model, so rests_on is empty.
Step 2: four dark grey 1x4 plates (3710) go around the edge of the black base plate b28, leaving a hollow in the middle. I could not read the exact layout from the picture.

Step 3: a white 2x4 plate (3020) fills the middle of the hollow, and three dark grey 2x2 plates go along the front edge. I took these as 3022, because the list has 4 grey 2x2 plates and the icon is a plain square.
The pictures do not show whether the step 3 plates also overlap the step 2 plates, so I listed only the base plate b28 under each piece.

Step 4: the second black 4x10 plate is added as a lower layer. The first base b28 and everything on it sits on top of b37, and b37 sticks out to the front and right. That is how I read the picture, where the new plate's studs show one level lower than the first plate's.
I have not changed b28's rests_on from the earlier page. The new plate b37 has nothing under it, so its rests_on is empty. The link between b28 and b37 is recorded in other_joins.

The unplaced-parts list suggests the four 1x4 plates from the previous page may have been Blue 3710 rather than Dark Bluish Gray, although the picture looks dark grey. I did not change the earlier entries.
Step 5: a tan 1x2 tile and two light grey jumper plates (3794b) go on the exposed front part of the lower black plate b37, between the grey 2x2 plates and the front edge.
Step 6: three green 1x1 plates and five light grey 1x1 tiles go along the front edge of b37, the green ones near the ends. I read it as a pavement or garden edge.
I put every piece on b37 only. The pictures do not show whether any of them also sit on the grey 2x2 plates from step 3.

Step 7 adds eight more pieces on the front part of the lower black plate b37: two tan 1x2 tiles (next to the earlier tan tile, they make a three-stripe walkway), two dark grey 1x2 tiles, two dark grey 1x3 tiles, and two green 1x3 plates (grass at the front corners).
I put every piece on b37 only. The pictures do not show exactly where each piece goes, and they do not show whether any of them also sit on the grey 2x2 plates from step 3.

Step 8: one dark grey 2x2 plate, three light grey 1x2 plates and two light grey 1x4 plates. I put the 2x2 and the two 1x4 plates on the upper base b28, and the three 1x2 plates on the lower plate b37. I could not read exact positions or what each piece overlaps from the pictures.

Step 9: two light grey 2x2 corner plates (2420) go on b28. Two reddish-brown round plates go on top of green 1x1 plates, one at the front-left corner and one at the back-right of the pavement. I took the two green 1x1 plates to be b41 and b42, but could not tell which of the three green plates each brown plate sits on.
The pictures do not show whether the step 8 and 9 pieces also overlap the earlier plates.

Step 10 adds two lime round plates, two yellow 1x1 plates, two clear 1x1 plates and one clear 1x2 plate. I took the clear pieces to be 3024 and 3023 in Trans-Clear, since the list has only that clear colour for those parts.

I put the lime plates on green pieces at the front corners, the yellow plates on the two light grey corner plates, and the clear plates on the light grey 1x2 plates at the front. This is a guess, because the picture is small and I could not tell exactly which piece each one sits on.
Step 11 builds a small stack three times: two clear 1x1 plates with a yellow 1x1 plate on top. One goes on the left of the building and two on the right. Each stack is one brick high.
Step 12 starts the back wall: a white 1x1 brick, a dark grey grille brick and a white 1x4 brick, all placed along the back row of the base.
The pictures do not show exactly which lower pieces each stack and wall piece sit on, so I picked the nearest plates from earlier pages. These links are guesses.
Step 13: a black 2x2 brick goes in the middle of the building, on the white plate area b33. A white Technic brick 1x2 with two pin holes goes at the left end, on the light grey plate b61.
I only listed the nearest plate under each brick. The black brick may also sit on other plates, which the picture does not show.
Step 14: a second white Technic brick 1x2 gets two black Technic pins pushed into its holes, then goes at the back-right corner of the building, with the pins sticking out sideways.
Step 15: two white 1x1 bricks go on at the right end of the back wall. I could not read exactly where, so I put them on the upper base b28. They may sit on other pieces as well.
The Technic brick is placed on b57, which is my guess at the plate in the back-right corner.
Step 16 builds a small stack: a red 1x2 plate, two clear 1x2 plates on it, and a red 1x2 tile on top. It then goes on the white plate b33, in front of the black 2x2 brick.
The picture shows two clear plates in the stack, but it is hard to tell whether the second one sits directly on the first. I assumed they stack directly.
Step 17 adds two blue 1x2 bricks, one on each side of the building (left front and right back), and two yellow 1x1 bricks, one on each side of the red counter.
Which plate each brick sits on is a guess. The blue bricks go on the two light grey corner plates, and the yellow bricks go on the white plate b33. The picture does not show the plates underneath.
Step 18 builds a stack of three clear 1x1 plates twice. One stack goes on the free stud of each blue 1x2 brick (b97 on the left, b98 on the right), the two spots the arrows point to.
I read the arrows as pointing at the blue bricks. The picture is small, so the exact spot could differ.
Step 19 adds two clear cheese slopes, two green flower plates and two green cones. The cones go on the two reddish-brown round plates as small trees. The flowers go on the two lime round plates.
The picture shows only one slope clearly, at the front-left on the clear plates. I put the second slope on the other clear 1x1 plate (b72). This is a guess.
Step 20 stacks two silver round plates and a silver round tile on top, like a short lamp post. It goes at the right of the front pavement.
I put it on the free stud of the right-hand light grey jumper plate b40. The picture does not make the exact spot clear, so that is a guess.
Step 21 lays the first roof layer: two white 2x4 plates (3020) at the left and right ends and one white 2x6 plate (3795) along the back.
The pictures do not show exactly which pieces each plate rests on, so I listed the wall pieces, towers and stacks nearest to it. Those lists are guesses.
Step 22: a yellow 1x4 tile bridges the two yellow 1x1 bricks over the red counter, like a shop entrance. Two blue 1x2 plates cap the blue bricks at the front.

I put each blue plate on its blue 1x2 brick (b97 on the left, b98 on the right). The clear plate stacks from step 18 sit on those same bricks, so the plates may in fact rest on the stacks instead. The picture does not settle this.
Step 23 puts a blue border on the white roof plates: two blue 1x4 plates and three blue 1x2 plates along the back, left and right edges.
The picture does not show exactly where each plate lies or what it overlaps, so the rests_on links are guesses. The blue plates go on the three white roof plates b116, b117 and b118.
Step 24 finishes the blue frame at the front of the roof: a blue 1x6 plate across the front, and a blue 2x2 corner plate at each front corner.

I read the 1x6 plate as resting on the two front blue plates and the yellow tile, and each corner plate as resting on a white roof plate plus the blue plate next to it. The picture does not make this certain, so these links are guesses.
Step 25 adds four white 1x4 bricks on top of the blue roof border, making a raised white wall along the left, back and right.
The exact layout is hard to read, so the rests_on links to the blue border plates (b122 to b126) are guesses.
Step 26 adds two tan 1x4 bricks side by side along the back, just inside the white wall.
